exposure: Carprofen administration (4 mg/kg sc followed by 2 mg/kg po every 12h)
Condition type (cesarean section, painful inflammatory conditions, mastitis)
outcome: Theoretical maximum total daily intake of carprofen by puppies
Computerized simulation of plasma concentration of carprofen in puppies
cohort: The study enrolled 100 lactating bitches, including 88 after cesarean section, 8 with painful inflammatory conditions, and 4 with mastitis, along with their puppies.
finding: The major finding was that carprofen concentration in milk was <700 ng/mL from bitches after cesarean section or with painful inflammatory conditions (other than mastitis), resulting in simulated puppy plasma concentrations one tenth of adult dogs, whereas mastitis led to higher concentrations (up to 1300 ng/mL).
mod_finding: The concentration of carprofen in milk was less than 700 ng/mL in bitches undergoing cesarean section, indicating a low excretion into milk and providing an analgesic alternative.
